slot.brief: check coplanarity of three vectors (or points) via the scalar triple product / determinant being zero and find the missing parameter

stem: If the line of intersection of the planes $2x - y = 1$ and $3y - 2z = 1$ is coplanar with the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z}{p}$, then the value of $p$ is

verdicts.working: The first line passes through (1,1,1) with direction (1,2,3). The second passes through (1,0,0) with direction (1,2,p). Coplanarity requires (0,-1,-1)·[(1,2,3)×(1,2,p)] = p−3 = 0, so p=3.

working:
Normals: $\mathbf{n_1}=(2,-1,0)$, $\mathbf{n_2}=(0,3,-2)$. Direction of intersection line $L_1$: $\mathbf{d_1} = \mathbf{n_1} \times \mathbf{n_2} = (2,4,6) \parallel (1,2,3)$. A point on $L_1$: put $x=0 \Rightarrow y=-1,\ z=-2$, so $A(0,-1,-2)$. $L_2$: passes through $B(1,0,0)$, direction $\mathbf{d_2}=(1,2,p)$. $\mathbf{AB} = (1,1,2)$. Coplanarity: $[\mathbf{AB},\mathbf{d_1},\mathbf{d_2}]=0$: $$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \ 1 & 2 & 3 \ 1 & 2 & p \end{vmatrix} = 1(2p-6)-1(p-3)+2(2-2) = p-3=0 \Rightarrow p=3.$$

Independent check: The first line passes through (1,1,1) with direction (1,2,3). The second passes through (1,0,0) with direction (1,2,p). Coplanarity requires (0,-1,-1)·[(1,2,3)×(1,2,p)] = p−3 = 0, so p=3.
solution:
The intersection line has direction $\mathbf d_1=(2,-1,0)\times(0,3,-2)\parallel(1,2,3)$ and passes through $A(0,-1,-2)$. The second line passes through $B(1,0,0)$ with direction $\mathbf d_2=(1,2,p)$.
For coplanarity, $\overrightarrow{AB},\mathbf d_1,\mathbf d_2$ must be coplanar, so
$$\begin{vmatrix}1&1&2\\1&2&3\\1&2&p\end{vmatrix}=p-3=0.$$
Hence $p=3$.
